Implement the following plan:

# Slice 5.2 — grant table + `SYS_SETGRANT` / `SYS_SAFECOPY` / `SYS_COPY`

## Context

Phase 5's deliverable is a filesystem-backed `exec` of a musl binary. Every byte
that crosses a process boundary on that path — VFS reading a path string, TTY
transmitting a user's `write()` buffer, MFS returning file data, the kernel
loading an ELF staged by VFS — needs a governed way to move memory between
address spaces. Decision **D4** (`docs/plans/phase-5-musl-fs.md`) settles that as
real MINIX-style grants rather than an interim shortcut: each granting process
keeps a grant table in its own address space, registers it with `SYS_SETGRANT`,
and `SYS_SAFECOPY` resolves + validates a grant id before copying.

Slice 5.1 already built the hard half. `kernel/src/mm/uaccess.rs` moves bytes by
explicit page-table walk through the HHDM (`walk_pt_in`), never by dereferencing
a user VA — so a cross-address-space copy is two walks and a `memcpy`, an
unmapped page is `EFAULT` rather than an EL1 abort, and no exception-fixup table
is needed. `Priv::grant_table` / `grant_entries` have existed unused since slice
2.2. `SYS_SETGRANT` / `SYS_SAFECOPY` / `SYS_COPY` are already numbered
(`0x605`/`0x606`/`0x60D`) and `ENOSYS`-stubbed in `kernel/src/system/stubs.rs`,
and are already granted to every server by the `SRV_T` `k_call_mask` fill — so
this slice adds **no new kernel-call numbers** and needs **no new priv wiring**.

Outcome: two boot servers move bytes across address spaces through a validated
grant, and the same engine backs the raw `SYS_COPY` control-plane read. Slices
5.3–5.9 (CDEV write, VFS write path, MFS reads, grant-sourced `SYS_EXEC`) all
build on this.

## Decisions taken in planning

1. **The grant id reaches its consumer in-band, not through DS.** The slice
   sketch said "publish the grant id through DS (`grant.test`)", but `DS_PUBLISH`
   deliberately registers the kernel-stamped `m_source` and ignores the payload
   (its anti-spoof property), so it cannot carry an id today; and an
   init-ordering handoff through DS races. Instead VFS `ipc_send`s PM a
   `PM_GRANT_TEST` message carrying `{granter, grant_id, len, addr}`. SEND blocks
   until PM's loop receives it, so the demo is self-synchronizing — and this is
   how grant ids really travel (slice 5.3's `CDEV_WRITE {minor, granter,
   grant_id, len}` is the same shape). Cost: one demo-only PM request number,
   retired when a real consumer lands.
2. **Magic grants get a live QEMU proof**, not just host tests — otherwise the
   arm is dead code until 5.5. PM magic-grants init's text page
   (`0x0010_0000`, the load base every user binary shares) to itself and
   safecopies 8 bytes out of init's address space. Uses only init's endpoint,
   which PM already holds in `mproc`; no new protocol.
3. **`SYS_COPY` is proved in the same demo.** The `PM_GRANT_TEST` message
   already carries VFS's raw buffer address, so PM additionally `SYS_COPY`s the
   same 64 bytes without a grant and compares checksums — precisely D4's "small
   control-plane read" shape.

## Scope

### `kernel-shared` — the grant ABI (host-tested)

New `kernel-shared/src/grant.rs`, re-exported from `lib.rs`:

- `GrantEntry`, `#[repr(C)]`, **flat** (no union — D4): `flags: u32`, `seq: u32`,
  `who_to: Endpoint`, `who_from: Endpoint`, `addr: u64`, `len: u64`. 32 bytes,
  align 8; pin both with `const _: () = assert!(...)` and `offset_of!` asserts,
  the way `ipc/message.rs` pins its payload offsets — a field inserted ahead of
  `addr` would otherwise be a silent misread by the kernel.
- CPF flags at MINIX 3 `include/minix/safecopies.h` values: `CPF_READ` 0x1,
  `CPF_WRITE` 0x2, `CPF_TRY` 0x10 (reserved, unimplemented), `CPF_USED` 0x100,
  `CPF_DIRECT` 0x200, `CPF_INDIRECT` 0x400 (reserved → `EINVAL`), `CPF_MAGIC`
  0x800, `CPF_VALID` 0x1000.
- Grant-id packing at MINIX's `GRANT_SHIFT = 20` (seq in the upper 11 bits, idx
  in the lower 20): `grant_id(idx, seq)`, `grant_idx(g)`, `grant_seq(g)`,
  `GRANT_MAX_IDX`, `GRANT_MAX_SEQ`, `GRANT_INVALID = -1`, `grant_valid(g)`.
  Round-trip and boundary tests.

In `kernel-shared/src/message.rs`, beside `page_chunks` (same rationale — the
kernel crate has no `#[cfg(test)]` and this is where the off-by-one risk lives):

- `dual_page_chunks(src_va, dst_va, len)` → iterator of
  `{src_page_va, src_offset, dst_page_va, dst_offset, len}`, stepping by
  `min(src_to_page_end, dst_to_page_end, remaining)`. Tests: aligned, src-only
  straddle, dst-only straddle, both straddling at different offsets,
  contiguity/total-length, `len == 0`.

In `kernel-shared/src/callnr.rs`: `SAFECOPY_FROM = 1` / `SAFECOPY_TO = 2`
(0 invalid, the `VMCTL_*` convention) plus doc comments giving the three payload
layouts, and `PM_GRANT_TEST = PM_RQ_BASE + 5` with `NR_PM_MSGS` 5 → 6.

Payload layouts (offsets within `Message::payload`; `u64` fields land 8-aligned
relative to the message base):

| call | 0..4 | 4..8 | 8..12 | 16..24 | 24..32 | 32..40 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `SYS_SETGRANT` | — | entries (i32) | — | table VA (u64) | — | — |
| `SYS_SAFECOPY` | direction | granter ep | grant id | grant offset | caller addr | bytes |
| `SYS_COPY` | src ep | dst ep | — | src addr | dst addr | bytes |

### Kernel — the copy engine

`kernel/src/mm/uaccess.rs` gains one function beside the 5.1 trio:

```rust
pub fn copy_between_as(src_ttbr0: u64, src_va: u64,
                       dst_ttbr0: u64, dst_va: u64, len: usize) -> Result<(), i32>
```

Probe both ranges first (`probe_user_range(src, .., false)` then
`probe_user_range(dst, .., true)`), then walk-and-`memcpy` per
`dual_page_chunks`. All-or-nothing on the destination, exactly the 5.1 contract,
and `Prot::writable` on the destination is load-bearing for the same reason (the
HHDM alias is a kernel mapping the MMU's EL0 permission bits do not police).

### Kernel — the three handlers

Delete `do_copy` / `do_safecopy` / `do_setgrant` from
`kernel/src/system/stubs.rs` (leaving `do_irqctl` / `do_times`) and add:

- **`system/do_setgrant.rs`** — caller-local in spirit but needs `&mut Priv`, so
  it is routed from the target-taking `match` in `kernel_call_dispatch` (which
  holds `&mut [Priv; NR_SYS_PROCS]`), like `do_kill`. Validates with the existing
  `user_va_ok(addr, entries * size_of::<GrantEntry>())`, then records
  `(grant_table, grant_entries)`. **Rejects a shared priv slot** —
  `caller_priv.proc_nr != Some(caller_nr)` → `EPERM`. Unreachable today (the
  shared `USER_PRIV_ID` has an empty `k_call_mask`), but without it a future
  grant-capable user class would have every process sharing one table address.
  `entries == 0` clears the registration.
- **`system/do_safecopy.rs`** — `verify_grant` + `do_safecopy`, both taking the
  `proc_table` + `priv_table` slices + `caller_nr`. `verify_grant` resolves the
  granter through `table::okendpt` (stale generations → `EDEADSRCDST`, the
  existing convention), returns `EPERM` when the granter has no table or the idx
  is out of range, reads the entry out of the *granter's* address space with
  `copy_from_user_as(granter.ttbr0_pa, table + idx * 32, ..)` — a walk miss is
  `EFAULT`, hidden as `EPERM` the way MINIX hides a bad granter table — then
  checks, in MINIX's order: `CPF_USED | CPF_VALID` set, `seq` matches the id's
  seq, requested access ⊆ `flags`, grantee endpoint matches the caller,
  `offset + bytes` neither overflows nor exceeds `len`. `CPF_DIRECT` resolves the
  source AS to the granter; `CPF_MAGIC` resolves it to `who_from` and
  additionally requires the granter's `Priv::flags & SYS_PROC` — minix.rs's
  variant of MINIX's hardcoded "only VFS and MIB may do magic grants", so the
  gate is the existing server-grade marker rather than a proc-nr list.
  `CPF_INDIRECT` returns `EINVAL` with a comment naming the deferral (D4).
  `do_safecopy` then picks src/dst by direction and calls `copy_between_as`.
- **`system/do_copy.rs`** — raw privileged copy on the same engine: resolve both
  endpoints via `system::resolve_target` (so `SELF` works), reject a zero
  `ttbr0_pa` (kernel task / unset slot) with `EINVAL`, `copy_between_as`. No
  grant, no per-target authorization — `k_call_mask` is the gate, the documented
  `do_vmctl` trust stance, and the module header says so.

Dispatch: add `SYS_SETGRANT` / `SYS_SAFECOPY` / `SYS_COPY` arms to the
target-taking `match` in `system::kernel_call_dispatch` and drop them from
`dispatch_caller_local`. `NR_KERN_CALLS` stays 18, so
`dispatch_caller_local`'s const assert is untouched.

Teardown: in `system/do_exit.rs`'s slot teardown, clear `grant_table` /
`grant_entries` when the priv slot is dedicated to the dying proc
(`priv.proc_nr == Some(nr)`), so a recycled server slot cannot inherit a stale
table address.

Traces, head-carved like `do_vmctl`'s `VMCTL_TRACE_HEAD` (a sampled trace would
miss these low-rate callers — see the QEMU-forensics note in CLAUDE.md):
`[ksys SYS_SETGRANT] proc=… entries=…`, `[ksys SYS_SAFECOPY] granter=… gid=… bytes=…`,
`[ksys SYS_COPY] src=… dst=… bytes=…`.

### `server-rt` — the grant client

New `server-rt/src/grant.rs`, exported from `lib.rs`. **`server-rt` keeps
`#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`** — the table is not a static, it is a value the server
owns:

```rust
pub struct GrantPool<const N: usize> { entries: [GrantEntry; N], next_seq: u32, registered_at: u64 }
```

- `grant_direct(who_to, addr, len, access) -> Result<i32, i32>`,
  `grant_magic(who_to, who_from, addr, len, access)`, `revoke(gid)`.
- `ensure_registered(&mut self)` compares `(&raw const self.entries) as u64`
  against `registered_at` and re-issues `SYS_SETGRANT` if they differ — creating
  a raw pointer and casting it to an integer are both safe operations, so no
  `unsafe` is needed, and comparing addresses makes the pool self-healing if it
  is ever moved rather than silently pointing the kernel at freed stack.
- Sizing note for callers: a server's stack is one page, so keep `N` small
  (the demo uses 8 = 256 bytes).
- The allocation / seq-bump / revoke logic is factored into pure `*_in` helpers
  over `&mut [GrantEntry]` and host-tested (the `ds/registry.rs` shape); only
  `ensure_registered` traps, and it joins the coverage exclusions alongside
  `sef.rs` / `ds.rs` / `diag.rs`.

### The demo

**VFS** (`servers/vfs/src/main.rs`), in `main()` *after* `sef_startup` returns
and before the receive loop (not in `init_fresh` — the pool is a `main`-frame
value that does not exist yet inside `sef_startup`):

```
static GRANT_TEST_BUF: [u8; 64] = /* deterministic pattern */;
let gid = grants.grant_direct(PM_EP, &raw const GRANT_TEST_BUF as u64, 64, CPF_READ)?;
ipc_send(PM_EP, { m_type: PM_GRANT_TEST, granter: vfs_ep, gid, len: 64, addr })
```

A `static` (not `static mut`) lands in `.rodata`, which the ELF loader maps
read-only — correct for a `CPF_READ` grant and safe to address.

**PM** (`servers/pm/src/main.rs`) gains a `PM_GRANT_TEST` arm:

1. `SYS_SAFECOPY(SAFECOPY_FROM, granter, gid, offset 0, own buffer, 64)` →
   checksum A.
2. `SYS_COPY(src = {vfs_ep, addr}, dst = {SELF, own buffer}, 64)` → checksum B.
3. Magic: `grant_magic(who_to = PM, who_from = boot_endpoint(INIT_PROC_NR),
   addr = 0x0010_0000, len = 8, CPF_READ)` then
   `SYS_SAFECOPY(SAFECOPY_FROM, granter = PM, gid, 0, buf, 8)` — a genuine
   third-party cross-AS read out of init's page tables.
4. `diag_print` one line per result, with **stable** assertable prefixes and the
   run-variable values after them: `grant.test ok sum=…`, `copy ok match=1`,
   `magic ok len=8`. Init's `_start` bytes change whenever init is rebuilt, so
   the magic line asserts success, never the word value.

VFS's `ipc_send` blocks until PM's loop receives, so no ordering assumption is
made about SEF init; PM boots after VFS in the MXBI archive, and no cycle exists
(VFS's own init only SENDRECs DS).

### Generated C headers

Add the CPF flags, `GRANT_SHIFT` / `GRANT_MAX_*` / `GRANT_INVALID`, the
grant-id macros, and `SAFECOPY_FROM` / `SAFECOPY_TO` to
`tools/gen-c-headers/src/callnr_h.rs`, beside the `DIAGCTL_CODE_*` block, with
the usual renders-from-live-constants tests. The `GrantEntry` **struct** is
deliberately not emitted yet — no C consumes it before slice 5.6, and a fifth
header (`minix/safecopies.h`) would need its own builder + CI clang check.

### Docs

- `docs/plan.md`: flip **5.1** to `✓ shipped (PR #41, merged 2026-07-25)` (the
  `◀ ready` marker is stale — it merged as `e9582e9`) and **5.2** to `◀ ready`,
  slide `◀ next` to 5.3.
- `docs/plans/phase-5-musl-fs.md`: same marker moves, plus an **As built**
  section under slice 5.2 recording the three planning decisions above, the
  `forbid(unsafe_code)`-preserving `GrantPool` shape, the `SYS_PROC` magic gate,
  and the shared-priv-slot `SYS_SETGRANT` rejection.
- `CLAUDE.md`: one conventions bullet for the grant model, in the register of the
  existing slice bullets.
- `tests/qemu-boot.expected`: the new `[diag pm]` and `[ksys …]` markers.

## Critical files

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `kernel-shared/src/grant.rs` | **new** — `GrantEntry`, CPF flags, id packing, tests |
| `kernel-shared/src/message.rs` | `dual_page_chunks` + tests |
| `kernel-shared/src/callnr.rs` | `SAFECOPY_*`, `PM_GRANT_TEST`, `NR_PM_MSGS` 5→6 |
| `kernel/src/mm/uaccess.rs` | `copy_between_as` |
| `kernel/src/system/do_setgrant.rs` `do_safecopy.rs` `do_copy.rs` | **new** handlers |
| `kernel/src/system/mod.rs` | route the three into the target-taking `match` |
| `kernel/src/system/stubs.rs` | drop the three `ENOSYS` stubs |
| `kernel/src/system/do_exit.rs` | clear a dedicated priv's grant registration |
| `server-rt/src/grant.rs` | **new** — `GrantPool`, pure `*_in` helpers + tests |
| `servers/vfs/src/main.rs`, `servers/pm/src/main.rs` | the demo |
| `tools/gen-c-headers/src/callnr_h.rs` | CPF/grant constants |
| `tests/qemu-boot.expected`, `sonar-project.properties` | markers, coverage exclusion |

## Reuse (do not re-derive)

- `mm/uaccess.rs`: `copy_from_user_as` / `copy_to_user_as` / `probe_user_range`
  and `addrspace::walk_pt_in` — the whole cross-AS mechanism already exists.
- `message.rs`: `user_va_ok`, `page_chunks` / `PageChunk` / `USER_PAGE_SIZE`.
- `system::resolve_target` and `proc::table::okendpt` for every user-supplied
  endpoint.
- `proc::flags::SYS_PROC` as the server-grade marker for the magic gate.
- `servers/ds/src/registry.rs` for the pure-`*_in`-helpers-plus-thin-wrapper
  shape the `GrantPool` tests follow.
- `system/do_vmctl.rs` for the head-carved trace pattern and the trust-model
  header comment.

## Verification

Host gates (all must be green before pushing):

```sh
cargo fmt --all --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo clippy -p minixrs-kernel --target aarch64-unknown-none -- -D warnings
cargo clippy -p minixrs-kernel --target aarch64-unknown-none --no-default-features -- -D warnings
cargo test -p minixrs-kernel-shared -p minixrs-server-rt -p minixrs-gen-c-headers -p minixrs-pm
cargo gen-c-headers            # then clang -fsyntax-only, as the c-headers CI job does
```

QEMU (the primary verification for kernel code):

```sh
timeout 25 cargo run -p minixrs-kernel --target aarch64-unknown-none --release > boot.log 2>&1
tools/check-boot-log.sh boot.log
```

Expect, in addition to the existing 24 markers: `[ksys SYS_SETGRANT]`,
`[ksys SYS_SAFECOPY]`, `[ksys SYS_COPY]`, `[diag pm] grant.test ok`,
`[diag pm] copy ok match=1`, `[diag pm] magic ok`. The forbidden list must stay
clean — in particular `!!! kernel exception (vector index`, which is what a
kernel dereference of a bad grant address would produce.

Stub-free regression, the guard slice 5.1 established for newly-surfaced
failures:

```sh
timeout 25 cargo run -p minixrs-kernel --target aarch64-unknown-none --release \
  --no-default-features > boot-nostubs.log 2>&1
grep -a '\[efault\]' boot-nostubs.log   # must be empty
grep -a '\[diag pm\]' boot-nostubs.log  # demo still fires (it does not depend on stubs)
```

Mutation checks (5.1's precedent — a validator no marker exercises is a
validator that can regress silently). Each of these, stubbed out one at a time,
must make a marker disappear:

- the grantee-endpoint check in `verify_grant` (point PM's demo at a grant whose
  `who_to` is VFS itself),
- the `seq` staleness check (safecopy a revoked id),
- the `SYS_PROC` magic gate,
- `copy_to_user_as`'s destination-writable check on the `SAFECOPY_TO` path.

Negative arms worth one host or QEMU probe each: `CPF_INDIRECT` → `EINVAL`,
out-of-range grant idx → `EPERM`, `offset + bytes > len` → `EPERM`, unmapped
granter page → `EFAULT`.

## Out of scope

Indirect grants (documented `EINVAL`), `CPF_TRY` soft faults, vectored
safecopy (`SYS_VSAFECOPY`), grant-sourced `SYS_EXEC` (slice 5.8), and any
`minix/safecopies.h` C header (slice 5.6, when C consumes it).

# Executing Plans

## Overview

Load plan, review critically, execute all tasks, report when complete.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the executing-plans skill to implement this plan."

**Note:** Tell your human partner that Superpowers works much better with access to subagents (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Codex App, Copilot CLI, and Gemini CLI all qualify; see the per-platform tool refs in `../using-superpowers/references/`). If subagents are available, use superpowers:subagent-driven-development instead of this skill.

## The Process

### Step 1: Load and Review Plan
1. Ensure an isolated workspace: use superpowers:using-git-worktrees to create one or verify the existing one
2. Read plan file
3. Review critically - identify any questions or concerns about the plan
4. If concerns: Raise them with your human partner before starting
5. If no concerns: Create todos for the plan items and proceed

### Step 2: Execute Tasks

For each task:
1. Mark as in_progress
2. Follow each step exactly (plan has bite-sized steps)
3. Run verifications as specified
4. Mark as completed

### Step 3: Complete Development

After all tasks complete and verified:
- Announce: "I'm using the finishing-a-development-branch skill to complete this work."
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch
- Follow that skill to verify tests, present options, execute choice

## When to Stop and Ask for Help

**STOP executing immediately when:**
- Hit a blocker (missing dependency, test fails, instruction unclear)
- Plan has critical gaps preventing starting
- You don't understand an instruction
- Verification fails repeatedly

**Ask for clarification rather than guessing.**

## When to Revisit Earlier Steps

**Return to Review (Step 1) when:**
- Partner updates the plan based on your feedback
- Fundamental approach needs rethinking

**Don't force through blockers** - stop and ask.

## Remember
- Review plan critically first
- Follow plan steps exactly
- Don't skip verifications
- Reference skills when plan says to
- Stop when blocked, don't guess
- Never start implementation on main/master branch without explicit user consent

## Locked design decisions

### D1. Console/stdio sink: minimal TTY server (TX-only), now

A real user-space TTY driver lands in Phase 5 — not a kernel printf shim as
the only console. Scope is deliberately minimal: **TX only, polling PL011**
(write `DR`, poll `FR.TXFF`), no interrupts. The kernel **pre-maps the UART
MMIO page (phys `0x0900_0000`) into TTY's address space at boot** with
Device-nGnRE attributes — TTY is a boot server, so this is a one-off boot
step like stack setup, and `AddrSpace` grows a device-memory mapping mode.
VFS routes fd 1/2 over a new CDEV band to TTY; TTY reads the payload via
grant (`SYS_SAFECOPY`) and writes the UART. Kernel messages keep using the
kernel's own writer; interleaving is acceptable (raw tick bytes already
interleave).

*Rejected:* `SYS_DIAGCTL` as the **only** console (no user-space driver ever
exercised in Phase 5 — but see D2, it still lands as the debug channel);
VM-mediated `VMCTL_MAP_PHYS` device mapping (more MINIX-authentic, revisit
for virtio-mmio in Phase 6); TX+RX with IRQ routing (`SYS_IRQCTL`, GIC → EL0
notification — nothing consumes input until the Phase 7 shell; deferred to
Phase 6 alongside virtio-console).

### D2. `SYS_DIAGCTL` becomes real, early — as the debug channel

Servers currently cannot print at all; every later slice needs observability
while TTY/VFS/grants are still under construction. `SYS_DIAGCTL` (MINIX 3
pedigree: `kernel/system/do_diagctl.c`) gets a body in slice 5.1 with an
**inline-payload** form — length + up to ~90 text bytes inside the 96-byte
message payload — so it needs *zero* user-copy machinery. A `server-rt`
helper loops longer strings. TTY/CDEV is the real stdio path; DIAGCTL is for
server bring-up debugging, exactly like MINIX's kernel message path.

### D3. Root image: MFS image in the MXBI archive + `memory` ramdisk over BDEV

The root filesystem is an **MFS-formatted image** built at compile time by a
new host tool (`tools/mkfs-mfs`), packed into the MXBI archive as a non-ELF
blob (`proc_nr = -1`, name `rootfs`). At boot the kernel **copies the blob
into freshly allocated RAM frames and maps them RW into the `memory`
driver's address space** (the archive copy in kernel `.rodata` stays
pristine; the RAM copy makes the 5.10 write path natural). MEM discovers
`(va, len)` via a new `SYS_GETINFO` selector. MEM serves the image over a
minimal **BDEV band** to MFS. This is the MINIX boot shape (`memory` driver
ramdisk) — Phase 6 swaps virtio-blk in under an unchanged MFS.

`tools/mkfs-mfs` is a host Rust binary sharing on-disk structs with the
`fs/mfs` library half, so the format logic is host-tested round-trip
(mkfs writes, mfs reader reads).

*Rejected:* MFS reading the image directly without BDEV (one fewer protocol
now, MFS rework when real block devices arrive); a cpio-style initramfs
unpacked by VFS (avoids MFS entirely — but MFS *is* the Phase 5
deliverable).

### D4. Grant model: real MINIX-style grants — direct + magic — plus `SYS_COPY`

Full MINIX shape, not an interim: each granting process keeps a **grant
table in its own address space** (`GrantEntry` array); `SYS_SETGRANT`
records `(addr, entries)` in the caller's `Priv` (the fields already exist);
`SYS_SAFECOPY` resolves a grant id, reads the entry from the *granter's*
address space, validates (kind, `CPF_READ`/`CPF_WRITE` access, grantee
endpoint, range, idx+seq staleness — MINIX `GRANT_SHIFT` packing), then
copies. Two grant kinds in Phase 5:

- **direct** — granter grants a range of its own memory to a grantee
  (server↔server, e.g. PM→TTY console writes);
- **magic** — a server-grade granter (VFS) grants one process's memory to
  another (TTY/MFS reading a *user's* buffer) — the real single-copy
  read/write data path. Gated on server-grade priv.

**Indirect grants are deferred** (documented `EINVAL` arm) — nothing in
Phase 5 re-grants a received grant.

`SYS_COPY` (raw privileged endpoint+addr copy, MINIX `sys_datacopy`) is
implemented on the same engine — VFS uses it for small control-plane reads
(e.g. fetching a path string from a caller).

**Copy engine + inherent fault safety:** all cross-address-space access goes
through **explicit page-table walks via the HHDM** — the kernel never
dereferences a user VA through the live TTBR0 for grant work. An unmapped
page is a walk miss, returned as `EFAULT`; no exception-fixup machinery
exists or is needed. Page-at-a-time: walk source frame, walk destination
frame, `memcpy` through HHDM aliases. (`AddrSpace` already promises all
table access is HHDM-based and works on non-active address spaces.)

`GrantEntry` is `#[repr(C)]` in `kernel-shared` (flat struct — flags, seq,
grantee, third-party endpoint, addr, len — no union needed for
direct+magic), with the CPF flag constants and id packing helpers,
host-tested.

*Rejected:* direct-only grants (double copy through VFS for every FS byte,
magic retrofitted later anyway); `SYS_COPY`-only interim (ungoverned byte
movement; the chunk-6 brief explicitly prefers real grants).

### D5. Fault-safe user copy: PT-walk replaces `read/write_volatile`

The chunk-6-mandated safety floor, first feature slice (5.1 — right after
the errno resequence so its `EFAULT` marker carries the final value from
day one). The same walk-via-HHDM technique from D4
replaces the two message-copy functions (`copy_msg_from_user` /
`copy_msg_to_user`): a bad user message pointer becomes **`EFAULT` in the
caller's `x0`**, never a panic. The deferred receive-side flush
(`flush_deliver_msg`, currently `let _ =` with a comment admitting the error
is dropped) surfaces failure as `EFAULT` in the *receiver's* parked `x0` —
the receiver asked for delivery to a bad buffer; the message is consumed.
`user_va_ok` stays as the cheap range/alignment pre-gate.

*Rejected:* a real `el1h_sync` handler + ELR fixup table (Linux-style
`extable`) — strictly more machinery for the same observable behavior, and
the PT-walk engine has to exist for grants anyway. Revisit only if message
round-trip cost ever matters (walks can be cached per dispatch).

### D6. ELF authority for FS-backed exec: the kernel keeps it

`boot_image/elf.rs` stays the single ELF loader. It is refactored over a
small **chunked-source abstraction** — read header/phdrs into stack buffers,
copy segment pages — with two sources: the existing boot-image byte slice,
and a **granted user-space buffer** (cross-AS page reads on the D4 engine).
`SYS_EXEC` gains a second payload form carrying `(granter, grant_id, len)`
alongside the existing name form (the name form stays for boot-embedded
regression). PM/VFS stage the file: VFS reads the whole binary from MFS into
a static exec buffer (capped; a compile-time assert covers `/bin/hello`),
direct-grants it to PM's exec flow. No kernel heap, no kernel staging.

The loader stays strict (page-aligned `p_offset`, W^X): user binaries are
linked to comply (see D13). Frame-exhaustion hardening (a `p_memsz` cap)
lands with the grant-source form, since exec input stops being
build-produced.

*Rejected:* a user-space loader in VFS/PM/VM (MINIX-authentic `libexec`
direction — needs map-into-third-party-AS surface through `SYS_VMCTL` and a
second loader implementation for the same milestone; revisit if Phase 7+
wants PIE/interpreters).

### D7. Errno ABI: classic-MINIX values (≡ Linux/musl), MINIX extras above 200

`error.rs` is renumbered once, as the **opening slice (5.0)** — before any C
exists *and* before any Phase 5 slice bakes an errno value into a trace
marker, so no later slice ever re-touches an expected line over a value
change:

- **POSIX block:** classic book-era MINIX values, which are identical to
  Linux/musl numbering for everything Phase 5 needs (EPERM 1 … EACCES 13,
  EFAULT 14, EINVAL 22, EDEADLK 35, ENOSYS 38 — negated in-kernel as today).
  Where classic MINIX and Linux ever diverge, **musl's value wins** (the
  point is that musl's stock `bits/errno.h` and `syscall_ret.c`'s
  `r > -4096UL` convention work unmodified).

**As built** (differences from the sketch above, recorded so later slices do
not rediscover them):

- **The grant id travels in-band, not through DS.** `DS_PUBLISH` deliberately
  registers the kernel-stamped `m_source` and ignores the payload — that is its
  anti-spoof property — so it cannot carry an id at all, and an init-ordering
  handoff through DS would race besides. VFS `ipc_send`s PM a `PM_GRANT_TEST`
  message carrying `{granter, gid, len, rw_gid, addr}` instead. SEND blocks until
  PM's loop receives, so the demo is self-synchronizing; and this is the shape a
  grant id really travels in (slice 5.3's `CDEV_WRITE {minor, granter, grant_id,
  len}` is the same). Cost: one demo-only PM request number (`PM_GRANT_TEST`,
  `NR_PM_MSGS` 5 → 6), to retire when a real consumer lands.
- **The magic arm gets a live QEMU proof**, not just host tests: PM magic-grants
  init's text page (`0x0010_0000`, the load base every user binary shares) to
  itself and safecopies 8 bytes out of init's address space — a genuine
  third-party read from a process that granted nothing. Uses only init's
  endpoint, which PM already holds. Without it the arm would be dead code until
  5.5. The line reports only the length; init's `_start` bytes change on rebuild.
- **`SYS_COPY` is proved in the same exchange**: PM re-reads the *same* bytes
  from VFS's raw address with no grant and compares checksums (`copy ok
  match=1`). That comparison is what proves the grant path moved the right bytes
  rather than merely some bytes.
- **`server-rt` keeps `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`.** `GrantPool<const N>` is a
  *value* the server owns (a `main`-frame local that outlives the receive loop),
  not a static — so there is no `UnsafeCell` and no `unsafe impl Sync`. It also
  makes registration self-healing: `ensure_registered` compares the pool's live
  address against the one last registered and re-issues `SYS_SETGRANT` when they
  differ, and both taking a raw pointer and casting it to an integer are safe
  operations. The pool must be built in `main`, not `init_fresh` — that frame is
  gone by the time a grantee safecopies.
- **Magic is gated on `Priv::flags & SYS_PROC`**, minix.rs's variant of MINIX's
  hardcoded "only VFS and MIB may issue magic grants" — the same trust boundary
  with no proc-nr list to keep in sync.
- **`SYS_SETGRANT` rejects a shared privilege slot** (`priv.proc_nr !=
  Some(caller)` → `EPERM`). Unreachable today (the shared `USER_PRIV_ID` has an
  empty `k_call_mask`), but one table address cannot describe several processes'
  memory, and this is what stops a future grant-capable user class inheriting the
  hole. `do_exit` correspondingly clears `grant_table` / `grant_entries` on a

All five findings were valid and are fixed. Verified re-green: fmt, three clippy gates, 29 test suites, `gen-c-headers` + clang on all three triples, 38/38 QEMU markers, stub-free boot clean.

## 1. PM confused deputy — real, fixed

The sharpest of the five. PM holds `SYS_COPY`/`SYS_SAFECOPY`; its clients (init, every forked child on the shared USER privilege) hold neither. A payload-supplied granter meant any of them could aim a privileged cross-AS copy at a third party through PM and read a checksum of the result off the console.

Fix is the DS lesson applied properly: **the granter is now `msg.m_source`**, and the granter field is gone from the payload entirely — layout is now `{gid, len, rw_gid, addr}`. A client can only ever name its own address space. PM additionally serves the arm only when `m_source` is VFS. The boot log confirms the substitution works end to end: `[ksys SYS_SAFECOPY] granter=1` now comes from the kernel stamp.

I recorded this in `CLAUDE.md` and the As-built notes as a rule binding slice 5.3+ — CDEV/BDEV/FS must not reintroduce a payload granter field.

## 2. `do_exec` grant leak — real, fixed

exec preserves the privilege slot while replacing the address space, so `grant_table` survived pointing at a VA that now belongs to the new image. `do_exec` takes `priv_table` and clears the registration at the point of no return, guarded by the same `proc_nr == Some(target)` dedicated-slot test `do_exit` uses.

One thing worth being straight about: **this arm is unreachable in today's boot.** The only exec'ing procs are init's forked children on the shared `USER_PRIV_ID`, which the guard skips. It goes live the first time a server execs. I've said so in the As-built notes rather than implying it's covered by a marker.

## 3. `revoke` and the moved pool — real, fixed

I'd underweighted this. A grant that goes stale is benign (garbage fails `CPF_USED`); a **revoke** that silently doesn't reach the kernel is not — the entry gets cleared in the moved pool while the kernel keeps honouring the old address. `revoke` now calls `ensure_registered` first, with an early-out when nothing was ever registered so `new()`'s "no kernel calls until the first grant" property holds.

## 4 & 5. Both mine, both fixed

The "five denials" comment predated the rodata and unmapped probes — now says seven and explains why two are `EFAULT` rather than `EPERM`. The `PM_GRANT_TEST` doc was rewritten for the new layout and now documents `rw_gid` plus the m_source rule and why it exists.

Implements decision **D4**'s grant model, live end to end between two boot servers. Every byte that crosses a process boundary on the Phase 5 path — VFS reading a path string, TTY transmitting a `write()` buffer, MFS returning file data — now has a governed way to move.

A granting process keeps its `GrantEntry` table **in its own address space** and registers `(addr, entries)` with `SYS_SETGRANT`; `SYS_SAFECOPY` reads the entry back out of the *granter's* address space on every call, so a granter revokes by writing its own memory and the kernel caches nothing that could go stale. No new kernel-call numbers and no new priv wiring — all three calls were already numbered and blanket-granted to servers.

## What's in

**`kernel-shared`** — new `grant.rs`: flat `#[repr(C)] GrantEntry` (32 B, layout pinned by `offset_of!` asserts since the kernel decodes it from raw bytes), MINIX's CPF flag values, `GRANT_SHIFT = 20` id packing. `message.rs` gains `dual_page_chunks` and `user_range_ok`. `callnr.rs` gains `SAFECOPY_FROM`/`_TO`, `PM_GRANT_TEST`, `NR_PM_MSGS` 5 → 6. 68 → 91 tests.

**Kernel** — `mm::uaccess::copy_between_as`: probe both ranges, then walk-and-`memcpy` per dual chunk. All-or-nothing on the destination, and its `Prot::writable` check is load-bearing — a granter may *lie* about writability, and the HHDM alias is a kernel mapping the MMU's EL0 bits do not police. `do_setgrant.rs` / `do_safecopy.rs` / `do_copy.rs` replace the three `ENOSYS` stubs.

**`server-rt`** — `GrantPool<const N>` as a value the server owns rather than a static, which is what keeps the crate `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`.

**Demo** — VFS direct-grants PM a checksummed `.rodata` buffer and hands the id over in-band; PM reads it through the grant, re-reads the same bytes with the ungranted `SYS_COPY` and compares checksums, and magic-grants itself init's text page for a genuine third-party read.

## Decisions worth flagging

**The grant id travels in-band, not through DS.** `DS_PUBLISH` deliberately registers the kernel-stamped `m_source` and ignores the payload — that is its anti-spoof property — so it cannot carry an id at all. This is also the shape a grant id really travels in (5.3's `CDEV_WRITE {minor, granter, grant_id, len}`).

**The granter is `m_source`, never a payload field.** PM holds `SYS_COPY`/`SYS_SAFECOPY` and its clients (init, every forked child on the shared USER privilege) hold neither, so a caller-supplied granter endpoint would let any of them aim a privileged cross-address-space copy at a third party *through PM* — a confused deputy. **CDEV/BDEV/FS must not reintroduce a payload granter field.**

**`user_range_ok` is new** (not in the slice sketch). `user_va_ok` demands 8-alignment, which is right for the grant table but wrong for the byte buffers safecopy moves — and something has to bound `len` before `page_chunks` sees it.

**Magic is gated on `Priv::flags & SYS_PROC`**, minix.rs's stand-in for MINIX's hardcoded VFS/MIB list — the same trust boundary with no proc-nr list to keep in sync.

**Both `do_exit` and `do_exec` clear a dedicated slot's grant registration** — exit so a recycled slot cannot inherit a stale table address, exec because the registered VA describes the image being discarded while the privilege slot survives.

## Verification

Host gates all green: `fmt --check`, three clippy gates, 29 test suites, `gen-c-headers` + `clang -fsyntax-only` on all three triples and the opt-in errno block.

QEMU: 38/38 markers (24 pre-existing + 14 new), forbidden list clean. Stub-free `--no-default-features` boot has no `[efault]` lines and the demo still fires.

**Seven denial probes** (`[diag pm] grant.deny ok n=7`) keep every validator exercised by a boot marker: wrong grantee, wrong access, stale sequence, out-of-range index, range overrun, a granter lying about writability over `.rodata`, and a grant over an unmapped page. Two findings recorded rather than papered over:

- the **index range check is not independently observable** — an id past the table makes the entry read fail first, so it is defence in depth rather than the observed cause;
- the **`SYS_PROC` magic gate cannot be probed at all** in this slice, because every process able to call `SYS_SETGRANT` is server-grade. Inverting the gate proved it is evaluated on the live path (`magic ok` → `magic FAIL rc=-1`); the real negative probe belongs with the musl slices, and the `do_exec` grant-clearing arm is likewise unreachable until a *server* execs.

## Out of scope

Indirect grants (documented `EINVAL`), `CPF_TRY` soft faults, vectored safecopy, grant-sourced `SYS_EXEC` (5.9), and any `minix/safecopies.h` C header (5.6, when C consumes it).

Committed, pushed, and PR opened: **https://github.com/minixrs/minixrs/pull/42**

- Commit `129f645`, GPG-signed (verified `G` against your key `9ADA06BB…`), on `feature/slice-5.2-grants` — never on main.

Two things to keep in view when you review:

**The confused-deputy fix reshaped the demo's wire format.** `PM_GRANT_TEST`'s payload lost its granter field entirely — PM takes the granter from the kernel-stamped `m_source`. I wrote that into CLAUDE.md and the phase plan as a rule binding 5.3+ rather than a one-off, because CDEV/BDEV/FS all carry grant ids and the same trap is available to each of them.

**Two code paths ship unexercised by any marker, and I'd rather say so than let the green boot log imply otherwise.** The `SYS_PROC` magic gate has no possible negative probe yet — every process able to call `SYS_SETGRANT` is server-grade — so I proved it live by inverting it rather than by a marker. The `do_exec` grant-clearing arm is skipped on every exec in today's boot, since init's forked children sit on the shared USER privilege; it goes live the first time a server execs. Both are noted in the As-built section.

I'll leave CI to run — say the word if you want me to check back on it or merge once it's green (regular merge, not squash, per your workflow).
